mainEntity.name: How hard is it to get started?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's a phone number, not a hardware install. You forward your existing line to Voco — about five minutes with your phone provider — with no new hardware, no apps, and nothing for your team to learn. You keep your number, and most venues are live the same day.

mainEntity.name: What can Voco do today, and what's coming?

acceptedAnswer.text: Today Voco does two live jobs: it takes bookings (already serving paying venues) and it handles takeaway and pickup orders. The front-of-house concierge is in active development, and a drive-thru capability is on the drawing board. Start with what you need now and switch the rest on as they ship — same agent, same voice.

mainEntity.name: Can I start with just bookings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — that's exactly how Voco works. Every venue starts with the live bookings capability, then turns on add-ons when they need them. They're capabilities of the same agent, not separate products to buy and wire up again.

mainEntity.name: What happens if Bella isn't sure what a caller wants?

acceptedAnswer.text: She doesn't guess. If a call is unclear — a tricky request, a name she can't quite catch — Bella takes the caller's details and a message and flags your team to call them back, so an uncertain moment becomes a callback rather than a wrong booking.
Yes. Bella speaks natural Australian English and is tuned for local suburb and street names — not an overseas call centre. It's one of the first things owners notice.

The live bookings capability is flat monthly pricing with a free week to try it — no per-call or per-cover fees. See the VocoTable page for current plans. As new capabilities ship, we'll price them honestly and only for what you switch on.
